the Society of Behavioral Medicine supports the USPSTF recommendation for lung cancer screening in individuals with a 30-pack year smoking history, who are current smokers or who have quit within the last 15 years, and who are between 50–80 years of age.

LDCT-based screening can be an effective tool to reduce mortality from lung cancer in high-risk populations; however, it must be integrated with evidence-based tobacco treatments, which have been shown to be effective in reducing the risk for lung cancer in high risk populations.
